clauses.text:
Executive ®rber,
i ordler to effect the more expeditious construction, remodeling, etc., of
the buildings for the Boston, Massachusetts, Baltimore, Maryland, Detroit,
Michigan, New Orleans, Louisiana, San Francisco, California, and Savannah,
Georgia, Marine Hospitals, the early completion of which in connection with
war activities, constitutes a National Emergency and by virtue of the provisions
of the Act of Congress approved March 4, 191 (,i9 Stat. 1192), entitled "An Act
Making appropriations for the Naval Service for the Fiscal Year ending June
3o, 1 91i8, arid for other purposes", whereby it is provided "that in cases of
National Emergency the President is authorized to suspend provisions of law
prohibiting more than eight hours labor in anly one dlay of persons engaged
upon work covered by contracts with the United States:
Provided further, that the wages of persons employed upon such contracts
shall be computed on a basic day rate of eight hours work, with over time rates
to be paid for at not less than time and one-half for all hours work in excess of
eight hours", I do hereby suspend the provisions of lawv prohibiting more than
eight hours of labor in any one (lay byv persons engaged in the construction, re-
modeling, etc., of the above mentioned structures.
This order will take effect from and after this (late.
WOODROW WILSON
Tni; \Vi-ITE HOUSE,
August 31, 1918.
[No. 2950.]
//(%'
